title: Maximum Product Subarray
statement:
You are given a list of integers that may include positive numbers, negative numbers, and zeros. A subarray is any contiguous run of elements from the list (it must contain at least one element).

Your task is to determine the largest possible value you can obtain by multiplying together all the numbers in some subarray of the given list.

Keep in mind that multiplying two negative numbers produces a positive result, so a subarray that looks unpromising because it starts or passes through negative values might actually combine with another negative value later to yield a very large product. Zeros act as a reset point, since any subarray whose product includes a zero will have a product of zero.

Design an approach that scans the list efficiently, tracking enough information as you go to correctly account for sign flips caused by negative numbers.

examples.explanation: Taking the entire array: 3 * -2 * 5 * -1 * 4 = 120. The two negative numbers cancel out their signs, and this full-array product beats any shorter subarray's product.
The zeros split the array into isolated segments [1], [-3, -4], and [2]. The segment [-3, -4] has product 12, which is larger than any other segment's product, so 12 is the answer.

constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix of nums fits within a 32-bit signed integer range
